page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Definition
steps.why: An osteon is a UNIT and not a single structure, so the definition has to list the parts that make one up.
common_mistakes: Defining only the Haversian canal. The osteon is the canal plus the rings of bone around it.
Writing that it is found in spongy bone. It is found in compact bone.
steps.memory_tip: One canal plus its rings makes one osteon, and compact bone is built of these units side by side.
steps.margin_note: Name the canal and the rings around it, then give the second name.

The osteon is also called the Haversian system.

steps.label: What it does
steps.why: Bone matrix is solid, so blood vessels can reach the bone cells only through these canals; that is why the osteon exists at all.
common_mistakes: Leaving out what the canal contains. The vessels inside it are what make the osteon a transport system.
steps.memory_tip: The canal is the road through solid bone: artery, vein, lymph vessel and nerve.
steps.margin_note: Say it is the unit of compact bone, then name what the canal carries.

lines.text: Osteon = the structural unit of compact bone
